Code Review by Qodo

🐞 Bugs (2) 📘 Rule violations (0) 📜 Skill insights (0)
1. The budget grace period can start late 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>note_refusal() timestamps a refusal after ledger.admit() has released its lock, and
>StateFile._change() permanently keeps whichever thread writes first. If the first refused request
>is paused before that write, a later refused request can supply the timestamp, delaying the
>harness’s grace-period deadline.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[hb/gateway.py[713]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/pull/5/files#diff-fef3562d0489296e808673921d86c962355faa436a870c5f670f6d49e9471f96R713-R713) > >```diff >+ self.gw.note_refusal() >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Admission decides exhausted under the ledger lock, but the timestamp is taken only after that lock
>is released. The state-file lock preserves the first caller to reach _change, while the
>orchestrator computes its deadline from that preserved timestamp.
>
> > [hb/gateway.py\[209-224\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/67dae12dfbf9f29b8a3367707c9e851ab4972d8a/hb/gateway.py/#L209-L224) > [hb/gateway.py\[275-292\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/67dae12dfbf9f29b8a3367707c9e851ab4972d8a/hb/gateway.py/#L275-L292) > [hb/gateway.py\[553-556\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/67dae12dfbf9f29b8a3367707c9e851ab4972d8a/hb/gateway.py/#L553-L556) > [hb/gateway.py\[704-714\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/67dae12dfbf9f29b8a3367707c9e851ab4972d8a/hb/gateway.py/#L704-L714) > [hb/orchestrator.py\[281-284\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/67dae12dfbf9f29b8a3367707c9e851ab4972d8a/hb/orchestrator.py/#L281-L284) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Concurrent exhausted requests can write the state file out of refusal order, so a later request starts the grace period. >## Fix Focus Areas >- hb/gateway.py[209-224] >- hb/gateway.py[553-556] >- hb/gateway.py[704-714] >## Recommended Fix >Capture and preserve the first refusal's timestamp as part of the serialized admission decision, then publish that value to the state file without allowing a later refusal to replace it. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/c082c5b9-95fb-40f1-a4d5-1b7caa691f3d?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/c082c5b9-95fb-40f1-a4d5-1b7caa691f3d)
2. The budget grace period can start early 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>Exchange._handle() records first_refusal_ms before its synchronous state-file save and before
>constructing the budget-refusal response. If that save or the request thread is delayed, the toolkit
>counts the delay against the 30-second grace period and can kill the harness before it receives the
>refusal.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[hb/gateway.py[713]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/pull/5/files#diff-fef3562d0489296e808673921d86c962355faa436a870c5f670f6d49e9471f96R713-R713) > >```diff >+ self.gw.note_refusal() >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The new timestamp is captured before _save() writes and replaces the file; only afterward does
>_local() reach _answer() and _send(). The orchestrator subtracts elapsed time since that
>timestamp from the grace period.
>
> > [hb/gateway.py\[269-286\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/67dae12dfbf9f29b8a3367707c9e851ab4972d8a/hb/gateway.py/#L269-L286) > [hb/gateway.py\[553-556\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/67dae12dfbf9f29b8a3367707c9e851ab4972d8a/hb/gateway.py/#L553-L556) > [hb/gateway.py\[710-716\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/67dae12dfbf9f29b8a3367707c9e851ab4972d8a/hb/gateway.py/#L710-L716) > [hb/gateway.py\[1019-1025\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/67dae12dfbf9f29b8a3367707c9e851ab4972d8a/hb/gateway.py/#L1019-L1025) > [hb/orchestrator.py\[276-284\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/67dae12dfbf9f29b8a3367707c9e851ab4972d8a/hb/orchestrator.py/#L276-L284) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The state timestamp is captured before the state write and refusal response are constructed, allowing gateway-side delay to consume the harness's grace period. >## Fix Focus Areas >- hb/gateway.py[553-556] >- hb/gateway.py[712-716] >- hb/gateway.py[1019-1025] >## Recommended Fix >Record the refusal time at the point used for the budget-refusal record, without placing a potentially slow state-file write between the timestamp and that decision. Preserve the first refusal when publishing concurrent updates. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/31a2c538-69ce-4106-934c-c426f03d8196?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/31a2c538-69ce-4106-934c-c426f03d8196)

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
